title: Check your understanding: Temporarily Saving Changes

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of temporarily saving changes?
options: `git stash` saves selected in-progress changes so you can move to other work. Stashes are local and temporary, and the default does not include untracked files unless requested.
Git automatically backs up every file, including ignored and untracked files, to a remote.
The operation grants every contributor write access to the hosted repository.
questions.answer_key: `git stash` saves selected in-progress changes so you can move to other work. Stashes are local and temporary, and the default does not include untracked files unless requested.
questions.explanation: `git stash` saves selected in-progress changes so you can move to other work. Stashes are local and temporary, and the default does not include untracked files unless requested.

questions.prompt: Which command is the most direct starting point for this lesson’s example?
questions.explanation: Use `git stash push -m "work in progress"` as the first inspection/action in the example, and then verify the result with the companion checks in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest general practice when working with temporarily saving changes?
options: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
Run the most destructive option first; the reflog guarantees every file can always be recovered.
Assume the local command also changed the remote and satisfied all hosting-platform policies.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
questions.explanation: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
